description:
FILED s448n (Opus round-6 agent N), from the #543 probes.  PRE-EXISTING; it
became VISIBLE when #543 made `open(F,"+<&=$fd")` work, because that is exactly
the probe perl's own t/io/open.t uses to check inheritance.

PERL: every descriptor perl opens above $^F (default 2) gets FD_CLOEXEC, so an
exec'd child does NOT inherit it.  Probed 5.40.3:

    open(my $fh, '<', $f) or die;
    printf "FD_CLOEXEC=%s\n", (fcntl($fh, 1, 0) & 1 ? 1 : 0);   # F_GETFD
        perl  FD_CLOEXEC=1
        PCL   (fcntl is not implemented at all -- see below)

t/io/open.t's ok_cloexec() is the live measurement: it fresh_perl_is()es a child
running `print open(F, "+<&=$fd") ? 1 : 0` and expects "0".  Under PCL the child
INHERITS the descriptor, so the fdopen succeeds and the row prints 1.  That row
(perl's test 116, "not inherited across exec") is a NEW honest failure as of the
#543 fix; it used to "pass" because the `+<&=` mode was unknown and the open
failed for an unrelated reason.  The same shape recurs at perl's 124/128 and
throughout the file -- ok_cloexec is called after nearly every open.

TWO PIECES, and they are separable:

(a) SET IT.  Every fd PCL opens (files, pipes, sockets, accept, dup -- NOT the
    dup2 onto 0/1/2, which perl also leaves inheritable) should get FD_CLOEXEC,
    and `open(F,"<&=$fd")`-style fdopens should keep whatever the source had.
    sb-posix:fcntl with f-setfd / fd-cloexec is the call.  Watch the ORDER: a
    fork-pipe child needs its rewired 0/1 to stay open across the exec, so the
    flag must go on the PARENT's end only.

(b) `fcntl` IS NOT IMPLEMENTED -- `Undefined subroutine &main::fcntl called`.
    Perl code reads and sets the flag with it, and $^F ("Modification of a
    read-only value"? -- check) selects the threshold.  A test cannot even
    ASSERT (a) without it.

BAR: the fcntl probe above vs perl; a child-inheritance probe (open a file,
exec a PCL child that tries "+<&=$fd", expect failure); t/io/open.t's
ok_cloexec rows (perl 116/124/128) move ok; a Pl/t guard row.  Note the perl
rule is "> $^F", so descriptors 0/1/2 stay inheritable -- a guard that asserts
cloexec on STDOUT would be WRONG.


RULED s449 (Fable, 2026-08-29): the fcntl shape is SETTLED as this task describes -- sb-posix:fcntl f-setfd/fd-cloexec; perl-s > $^F threshold (0/1/2 stay inheritable); parent-end-only for fork-pipe rewiring; <&=$fd fdopens keep what the source had; piece (b) the fcntl builtin FIRST (returns "0 but true" for a 0 result), then (a).  Assigned to round-7 agent Q (s449q) in this launch.

subject: PCL sets no FD_CLOEXEC on the descriptors it opens, so every open handle leaks into an exec'd child (perl closes them; t/io/open.t "not inherited across exec")
